title: -na-autoload: exit the main menu after loading (menu-to-session transition)
description:
-na-autoload (thinker fork 2b82af5) successfully loads a savegame - mod_load_daemon returns SAVE_LOAD_VALID (status 0) against a real Autosave_<year>.sav, verified on the gaming host. But the game stays on the main menu, so the loaded state is unreachable.

Clearing *GameHalted is not sufficient. The engine does more of the menu-to-session transition inside load_game (engine.cpp:1057, address 0x5AAAB0) than state loading alone - probably tearing down the menu's own modal loop and entering the main interface. load_game takes (int, int) and addresses saves by slot, which is why it cannot be called directly for an arbitrary path.

Candidate approaches, cheapest first:
1. Identify what load_game does around its call to load_daemon (the call site is hooked at patch.cpp:639, address 0x5AAD7D) and replicate the surrounding steps. Disassembly of 0x5AAAB0..0x5AAD7D would answer it directly.
2. Find the menu's modal loop exit condition and set it alongside GameHalted.
3. Drive the menu with synthetic input instead. xdotool is installed and CAN see the Wine window ('Wine Desktop'), so sending the load-game keystrokes is feasible. Brittle and resolution-dependent, but it needs no engine RE and would unblock unattended runs today.

Approach 3 is the pragmatic unblock; 1 is the correct fix.
acceptance_criteria: Launching with -na-autoload <save> results in a playable in-game session with no human input; na-observations.jsonl shows base.production lines appearing without anyone touching the keyboard
notes:
PARTIAL. 0x58F450(1, arg2) after mod_load_daemon does clear GameHalted (rc=0, halted=0, verified) and the map renders at the correct year and faction. But it also raises a modal LOAD dialog over the session, and cancelling that dialog tears down to the main menu - so the session is NOT actually playable. Confirmed by the user at the machine; a screenshot showing a rendered map is misleading here, because rendered-behind-a-modal looks identical to loaded.

arg2 sweep so far: 0 and 1 both give rc=0, halted=0, and a blocking modal. Values 2 and -1 were queued.

Good automated test for this, no vision needed: after autoload, write 'shot' to the command channel. The channel is polled from ModWinProc, which stops being called during modal pumps, so a missing na-command-result means a modal is blocking. That distinguishes 'in session' from 'in session behind a dialog' without a screenshot.

Read of it now: 0x58F450 is probably not the right entry point, or needs state set before it. The dialog it raises looks like the engine's own load prompt, which suggests the transition expects to drive the load itself rather than being handed an already-loaded state. Worth investigating:
  - 0x5ADCE4, the OTHER site that clears GameHalted - a different and possibly cleaner path.
  - What the menu's LOAD GAME button calls, and at what point load_game (0x5AAAB0) decides to prompt. If the prompt is skippable by pre-setting the filename buffer that load_game reads, calling load_game directly becomes viable.
  - Whether the transition must be invoked from the menu's own context rather than from the window procedure.

Timing finding worth keeping regardless: a 3s gate reported total success and still showed the menu, because the engine's startup drew the menu over the entered session. 12s is past startup on this host. Any fix needs to fire after startup settles, and a real idle signal would be better than a timer.

title: Verify Steam terranx.exe is Alien Crossfire v2.0
description: Run sha1sum against the Steam Planetary Pack install; want 4b19c1fe3266b5ebc4305cd182ed6e864e3a1c4a (3,084,288 bytes). Thinker refuses any other build. If it differs, the physical ISO plus the official v2.0 patch becomes the primary fixture source. Blocks every game-dependent lane. See docs/headless-harness.md section 2.
notes:
RESOLVED on gaming host (2026-07-29), but NOT by matching the hash.

Steam Planetary Pack (app 2204130), installdir 'Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri':
  terranx.exe  sha1 7bbcc54e64760c11a24f48862f15dbaaeab61435  3,094,576 bytes
  terran.exe   sha1 ca90a0776a5685a01c346e85fd23f3116ece975e  3,201,128 bytes
  PE: i386, 8 sections, link timestamp 1999-12-20 20:30:55 (original Firaxis build, not repacked)

This does NOT match Thinker's documented GOG anchor (4b19c1fe3266b5ebc4305cd182ed6e864e3a1c4a / 3,084,288) - it is 10,288 bytes larger.

It works anyway. Thinker Mod v5.4 is already installed in this directory and has driven a real
game against this exact binary:
  - debug.txt records 'ModVersion Thinker Mod v5.4 (Apr 29 2026)' / 'BinarySize 3094576'
  - saves/auto/ holds a continuous autosave run to Autosave_2234.sav (2026-06-20 19:25-19:56)
Since patch.cpp:218,250 verify original bytes before patching and abort on mismatch, reaching
turn-by-turn play proves every patch site in this build matches v2.0.

Conclusion: the na-8p9 premise ('Thinker refuses any other build') was an overstatement of the
source. Technical.md's own allowance - 'using other official game binaries of the same version
should also work' - is the operative rule, and the Steam build is such a binary. The hash is a
GOG-specific anchor, not a compatibility gate.

Consequence for the fixture (na-dyt): the manifest must record THIS host's hashes as the Steam
provenance line and must not hard-fail on the GOG anchor. Treat the anchor as one known-good
value among several.

Bonus, for na-ie9: it ran under Proton, not bare Wine. Prefix at
~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/compatdata/2204130/pfx (ModuleName in debug.txt is the Wine
drive mapping S:\common\...). A working prefix already exists to build the Xvfb harness on.
close_reason: Steam build verified compatible empirically: sha1 7bbcc54e... / 3,094,576 bytes differs from the GOG anchor, but Thinker v5.4 patches and plays it (autosaves to year 2234). Fixture source settled as Steam; no ISO needed. See notes.

title: Enrich the base.production action space with cost and effect
description:
The action space must carry mineral cost, turns at current surplus, category (unit/facility/project) and a one-line effect for every offered item - not just a display name.

A bare name list is not a decidable comparison. 'Formers' vs 'Scout Patrol' cannot be weighed without cost, and a brain that cannot compare cost will systematically over-pick expensive items. This is the single highest-leverage input for decision quality on this surface (docs/decision-inputs.md section 1.1).

contract.Action is extra=allow, so the extra fields are additive and need no schema change. Ship cost and accumulated minerals separately and let the brain divide - do not pre-compute 'turns remaining' for a partially built item, which is where the arithmetic goes subtly wrong.
acceptance_criteria: Every Action in a base.production world view carries id, name, mineral cost, category and effect; the values are read from the engine, not hardcoded; a world view captured from real play is checked against the engine's own numbers
notes:
Landed in thinker fork: action space + base state emitted with every base.production observation. Engine-authoritative via can_build_unit/can_build; every action carries cost; facilities carry CFacility.effect from alphax.txt; projects distinguished by SP_ID_First; ids are unit:<proto>/facility:<id>. Base state ships accumulated minerals and surplus separately rather than a pre-computed turns-remaining.

NOT yet validated against a running game - the DLL is installed but applies on next launch. Validate: action_space_size is plausible (single digits early game), costs match the in-game build menu, facility effect strings are populated and not empty.
close_reason: Action space with cost/effect and base state landed in the thinker fork; validation against real play still pending (see notes).

title: mod_base_build fires twice per base per turn - decide which call is authoritative
description:
Measured in real play on 2026-07-29 (26 observations, turns 2-5, six factions): every (turn, base_id) pair appears EXACTLY TWICE in na-observations.jsonl, and the two calls return different choices. Gaia's Landing on turn 2 produced both 'Scout Patrol' and 'Formers'.

Cause: mod_base_reset is hooked at eleven engine call sites (thinker src/patch.cpp:859-869) - bases_reset, base_production x5, and four BaseWin entry points - and each calls mod_base_build (src/base.cpp:998).

Why this blocks A1 rather than being cosmetic: orchestrator.py owns 'exactly one decision record per decision, on every path'. If the adapter POSTs on every mod_base_build call, one base-turn produces two LLM decisions - double-counted coverage, double-billed tokens, and two contradictory orders for the same slot. The engine is authoritative about what it asks; we have to decide what constitutes one decision.

Thinker fork commit bd1a6ea now records has_gov (mod_base_build's own second parameter) on each observation so the two calls are distinguishable. Next step is to collect a longer sample and determine whether has_gov alone separates them, or whether the call site must also be identified (which would mean passing a discriminator from each patch site).
design: Candidate rules, cheapest first: (1) has_gov distinguishes them cleanly - filter on it; (2) last-call-wins per (turn, base_id), since the final call is what mod_base_change actually applies; (3) identify the call site by passing a constant from each of the eleven patch sites. Prefer (1) or (2) - (3) touches eleven hook sites and couples the adapter to engine layout.
acceptance_criteria: A rule is documented for which mod_base_build invocation is the decision of record; the adapter emits one observation per decision per base-turn, or emits all of them with a field that unambiguously marks the authoritative one; validated against a sample of at least 20 turns
notes:
VERIFIED in real play 2026-07-29, and the original framing was wrong in an important way.

Sample: 50 base.production records, turns 26-34, 38 distinct (turn, base_id) groups.

  call_seq values seen:      1 x38, 2 x10, 3 x2
  calls per (turn,base):     once x28, twice x8, three times x2
  call_seq unique in group:  38 of 38, zero collisions
  records with call_seq==1:  38 - exactly one per distinct base-turn

So gating on call_seq == 1 provably yields exactly one decision per base-turn. A1's
one-paid-call guarantee holds, and the invariant 'exactly one decision record per
decision' is satisfiable.

CORRECTION to the earlier finding. The title says 'fires twice per base per turn'.
It does not - it fires ONE to THREE times, and most often only once (28 of 38 groups).
The first sample happened to catch a turn where duplication was universal, which made
a variable phenomenon look constant.

This matters concretely: any rule of the form 'take the second call' or 'take the last
call' would have MISSED 28 of 38 decisions entirely, because for those groups there is
no second call. call_seq == 1 is correct precisely because it is the only invocation
guaranteed to exist for every base-turn. Had we settled on last-call-wins - which was
the leading theory and sounded principled - A1 would have silently skipped three
quarters of its decisions.
close_reason: Resolved and verified. call_seq is unique within every base-turn group (38/38, no collisions) and exactly one record per base-turn has call_seq==1, so gating on it gives one decision per base-turn. Also corrected the premise: the engine fires 1-3 times, not always twice, and most often once - so a last-call-wins rule would have missed 28 of 38 decisions.

title: K1: Quipu datalinks read path and static briefing
description: Implement Retriever against Quipu: smac shapes, alphax.txt to episode ingester, cached-once static briefing prompt-cached at game start. Exit: a Thinker static briefing is Quipu-sourced. Seam exists in knowledge.py; this fills it. knowledge-architecture.md K1.
close_reason: Landed less the Quipu round-trip. datalinks/ parses alphax.txt deterministically (no model: it is fixed-arity CSV with inline column docs, and a hallucinated tech prerequisite tagged canonical is the worst failure available to us), emits the smac: graph with all three anti-masquerade predicates on every node, and serves a static briefing plus action-space-scoped grounding through the Retriever seam. Verified against a real 1281-line alphax.txt: 88 techs, 133 facilities (50 Disabled), 64 SP rows, 2579 triples round-tripping through rdflib. Three bugs found by checking rather than eyeballing: (1) two facilities have commas inside effect text, so SP detection had to move from row arity to 'last five fields are ints'; (2) Turtle PN_LOCAL forbids '/', so smac:tech/biogen was a parse error that looked perfectly reasonable -- fixed with per-class prefixes and rdflib is now a dev dep gating it; (3) Disable in a preq column means excluded-from-game, not a prerequisite, and treating it as a tech would have invented 50 fake edges. Also: alphax.txt's own header calls the facility column 'Free' (grants the facility free at new bases), not obsoletedBy as knowledge-architecture.md says -- the file wins, noted in rdf.py. Added NA_EXTRACTION_MODEL (default claude-haiku-4-5) as a separate cheaper dial from the brain's, for K3's postgame episode extraction which IS genuine model work. Remaining: load the graph into a running Quipu and serve retrieval from it rather than the parsed structs -- folded into na-6ce (K2). 21 tests against a synthetic excerpt; the real alphax.txt is game data and is never committed.

Two gaps the LLM must own outright because no AI path runs for a human faction: energy sliders (game.cpp:1908 returns early) and social engineering (faction.cpp:1463 hard-returns). docs/thinker-adapter-notes.md section 5.0.

Mode B+ recommended and documented at the option in thinker.ini. Verified by MinGW cross-compile to a PE32 DLL. Intercepting an actual decision is A1 (na-61c).

title: A0 spike: log one mod_base_build decision under Wine
description: First real decision point observed. mod_base_build at thinker src/base.cpp:1145 is the cleanest seam: one int in, one int out, self-contained. Depends on the fixture and the harness.
notes:
Hook implemented and shipped: thinker fork commit 78a5af3 adds src/neural.{h,cpp} and calls na_observe_base_production from mod_base_build (src/base.cpp), gated on llm_enabled. Writes one JSON line per decision to na-observations.jsonl in the game directory, with surface_id=base.production, turn, faction, base, and Thinker's native choice. Observation only - native choice still executes, so no behaviour change.

Build and boot are verified: cross-compiles clean under i686 MinGW with -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow, produces PE32 i386, and drives the Steam terranx.exe under Wine 11.9 + Xvfb with the DLL attached (audio confirmed by Steve, so the game genuinely runs).

NOT yet verified: an actual observation line. mod_base_build only fires inside a running game, and a fresh boot sits at the main menu. Producing a line needs either a human to load a game and end a turn, or the -na-autoload flag from na-ie9. That is the only thing standing between here and closing this issue.
close_reason: DONE - observations confirmed in real play 2026-07-29. 26 lines in na-observations.jsonl across turns 2-5 and six factions, each with surface_id=base.production, turn, faction, base, coords, and Thinker's native choice. Full chain proven: fork cross-compiled on Linux, PE32 i386 DLL attached to the Steam Alien Crossfire terranx.exe under Wine, real game, real decision points logged. Note: the na-ie9 dependency was removed as mis-modelled - the spike needed a human to play one turn, not the unattended harness. Follow-up P1 filed: mod_base_build fires twice per base per turn; has_gov now recorded to disambiguate.

Hard timeout required: Thinker reports fatal errors via MessageBoxA, which under Xvfb hangs forever with nobody to click OK. Run windowed, not fullscreen. docs/headless-harness.md section 3.

Partially delivered as of 2026-07-29 (commit e78d07a + fork 78a5af3).

title: Neutralise or declare the fairness handicaps in the adapter
description: Map *DiffLevel and the conf.* values to a concrete per-faction handicap list and populate the world view fairness block. Six entries are difficulty-selected, nine are structural flat is_human branches. Policy is record not neutralise. docs/game-surface.md section 5.

Reading the source corrected the game-surface.md table in four places -- tech_cost_factor and content_pop flip sides at Librarian, combat modifiers favour the human not the AI, and unit_support_bonus is inert under shipped defaults. handicap_drift() catches an adapter whose stamp disagrees (missing/unexpected/mislabelled); coverage gained fair_play and structural_handicaps so the claim is measured. 25 new tests. title: Central mod_popp wrapper: intercept in-game dialogs as decision points
description:
Wrap the engine's dialog function popp(filename, label, a3, pcx_filename, fn) (engine.h:667) so every in-game dialog is visible to the adapter and routable to Claude.

This is invariant 7 made real: 'Intercept in-game dialogs; never blanket-suppress them. They are decision points.' Council votes, diplomacy offers, random events and pact proposals all arrive as popp dialogs, and each is a decision surface the brain should own. Only Thinker's fatal-error MessageBoxA should ever be suppressed.

Precedent exists: Thinker already hooks individual popp call sites - base_production_popp at patch.cpp:681 and BaseWin_staple_popp at 753-754 - so wrapping centrally is the same technique applied once instead of per site. Identify dialogs by (filename, label), which is what the call already passes.

IMPORTANT distinction, do not conflate these:
  - IN-GAME dialogs (events, diplomacy, council) are decisions. Intercept, emit a surface_id, route to the LLM tier where appropriate. Core architecture, and a whole class of surfaces at once.
  - MENU and file-picker chrome (the LOAD dialog) is not a decision, just startup plumbing. Do NOT build automation for it - fix the -na-autoload menu-to-session transition instead so no picker is ever needed. Automating the picker is throwaway work.

Note also that the LOAD picker is not a popp dialog and runs its own message pump, which is why the command channel goes deaf inside it (see na-abc).
acceptance_criteria: A single hook observes every popp dialog with its filename and label; each observed dialog is recorded with a surface_id; a documented allowlist controls which are auto-answered vs routed vs passed through to the human; Thinker's fatal-error MessageBoxA remains suppressed and nothing else is blanket-suppressed

title: Command channel goes deaf inside the engine's modal dialogs
description:
The in-DLL command channel (thinker fork, na_command_tick) is polled from ModWinProc. The engine's modal dialogs - the LOAD file picker among them - run their own message pump, so the window procedure stops being called and the channel stops responding while one is open. Verified: a 'shot' and a 'click' issued with the LOAD dialog open produced no result file at all.

The dialog is drawn INSIDE the game window rather than as a native Windows control (xdotool sees no separate X window for it), so it is not separately addressable from outside either. External input does not reach this game in any case - it reads the mouse through DirectInput under a Wine virtual desktop.

Consequence: automation can open a modal dialog but cannot act inside one. That is enough to reach the LOAD picker and no further, which is exactly one click short of useful.

Candidate fixes:
1. Hook something that runs during modal pumps. popp() and the Console/dialog handlers are the obvious candidates - find one that is unconditionally patched.
2. Avoid dialogs entirely: fix the -na-autoload menu-to-session transition so no picker is ever needed. That is the better goal and is tracked separately as the load_game transition bug.
3. A timer-based tick (SetTimer plus a WM_TIMER handler, or a worker thread) that survives modal pumps. A thread would need care - the engine is not thread-safe.

Approach 2 makes this issue moot for the resume use case, which is the only current consumer. Prefer it.
notes: Do NOT hook mod_blink_timer for this: it is only patched in when smooth_scrolling is enabled (patch.cpp:1166) and is absent with the default ini.

title: Add recent build history to the base.production world view
description:
Record what each base built over the last few turns and include it in the world view.

Production decisions are re-evaluated every turn (several times per turn at the engine level). A stateless brain will flip between two reasonable options turn after turn and accumulate nothing - each individual choice defensible, the sequence useless. Recent history is what makes a stable choice possible, and it is cheap: a short ring buffer per base.

Also record whether the current item was chosen by Claude or by the deterministic tier, so the brain can tell its own past reasoning from Thinker's.
acceptance_criteria: World view carries the last N items built or queued for this base, and the tier that chose the current one; verified across at least 10 consecutive turns of real play showing no oscillation between two options

title: just ingest should refuse a mod-contaminated alphax.txt
description:
The canonical ingester reads $SMAC_DIR/alphax.txt and tags the output canonical. If $SMAC_DIR points at a directory with Thinker installed over it, that file is Thinker's - house-rule data laundered into the canonical smac: graph, violating AGENTS.md invariant 4.

fixtures/smac/overlays.tsv already maps known mod hashes to their source, and scripts/game_fixture.py uses it to detect exactly this. Wire the same check into the ingest path: hash the input, and if it matches a known overlay, abort with a message pointing at just ingest-thinker instead. Cheap, and it closes the hole at the point of harm rather than relying on the operator remembering.
acceptance_criteria: ingest aborts non-zero with an explanatory message when given a file whose sha1 is in overlays.tsv; unit test covers it with no game data in the repo

title: Restore vanilla data files and resolve the 17 unresolved manifest paths
description:
fixtures/smac/steam-2204130.manifest is marked INCOMPLETE: 17 paths held Thinker v5.4 bytes when scanned and carry no vanilla hash - alphax.txt, german/alphax.txt, and 15 basenames/*.txt. Thinker was installed directly into the Steam directory and overwrote them (verified byte-identical to Thinker_v5.4.zip).

Needs a human action in the Steam client: Properties > Installed Files > Verify integrity of game files. That re-downloads tracked files and leaves untracked additions (thinker.dll, thinker.exe, smac_mod/) alone. Then run 'just game scan' to regenerate a complete manifest - it will now succeed without --allow-contaminated.

alphax.txt is the one that matters: 'just ingest' labels it canonical, so ingesting Thinker's copy would mislabel house-rule data as game-canonical (AGENTS.md invariant 4). Do NOT run 'just ingest' against the play directory until this is resolved. basenames/ and german/ are cosmetic and block nothing.
acceptance_criteria: just game scan succeeds with no --allow-contaminated flag; manifest header has no INCOMPLETE block; just game verify passes; just ingest produces a canonical smac: graph from vanilla alphax.txt
notes: Longer-term: $SMAC_DIR should be a pristine tree and the play directory a separate copy with the mod overlaid. See docs/headless-harness.md 2.4 and fixtures/smac/PROVENANCE.md.

title: Supply an embedding model so quipu_context works
description: Filed upstream as scbrown/quipu#53. quipu knot does not embed (only /episode does), --embed-backfill fails with 'No embedding provider configured', and --features onnx supplies the runtime not a model. Needs .bobbin/config.toml with model_path/tokenizer_path plus the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 files. huggingface.co is NOT on the Claude Code cloud Trusted allowlist, so either add it to a Custom allowlist or vendor the model. Exact-match SPARQL grounding is unaffected and works today.

title: Load the datalinks graph into Quipu and serve retrieval from it
description: Finishes K1: DatalinksRetriever currently reads parsed Python structs. Swap the lookup for quipu_context / a SPARQL query against the local store (just quipu-load) behind the same Retriever protocol, so the orchestrator does not notice. Verified reachable: quipu 0.3.11 built with shacl,onnx loads all 2579 triples and answers property-path queries. Overlaps na-6ce (K2); do this first.
close_reason: QuipuRetriever queries a running quipu-server over REST (POST /query, stdlib urllib, no new runtime dep) behind the same Retriever protocol as the struct-backed one, so swapping is a constructor argument. Read-side engine filter is mandatory with no bypass: emission tags appliesToEngine, but if retrieval does not filter on it the tag is decoration -- verified live, glsmac gets 0 hits where thinker gets 1. Non-canonical tiers ride into the prompt. One batched query per decision bounded to the action space, 2s timeout, proxies disabled for loopback, SPARQL literals escaped. BLOCKER FOUND: Quipu implements neither VALUES nor FILTER(?x IN (...)); knowledge-architecture.md, quipu-integration.md and strategy-knowledge.md all specified them. A || disjunction works; all three docs corrected and na-hgd filed. 20 tests, 4 live against quipu 0.3.11. Wired as NA_QUIPU_URL plus 'just quipu-serve'.

title: K6: Hank hot state graph, policy guard and what-if
description: Implement Guard against Hank: hot per-faction COW state graph, deny/warn policies, what-if over the live board. Gated behind new Hank spec FRs. K6, roles c/d/e.

title: K2: per-turn Quipu retrieval and budgeting
description: quipu_context plus action-space grounding via one batched SPARQL VALUES query over this turn's action_space, plus hybrid-search tactics k=3 confidence-gated. Token budget: drop tactics before rules. Degradation already handled by the seam. K2.
close_reason: Split: the budgeting half landed, the semantic half is blocked and now has its own bead. Landed: datalinks/budget.py enforces an approximate token ceiling and sheds tactics before rules -- rules are correctness, tactics are optimization, and that ordering is the same precedence the prompt enforces, so the budget cannot invert the trust ordering to save tokens. A single greedy pass in list order would have let a long tactic at the front crowd out a rule behind it, so it fills by precedence class instead, and it keeps scanning past an oversized fact since a later shorter one may still fit. Nothing is dropped silently: the surviving grounding carries an explicit '[N tactics omitted for token budget]' line, because a truncated prompt that reads as complete is the same failure shape as the all-fallback run. Wired as QuipuRetriever(token_budget=N), default 0 = unbounded since the action-space cap already bounds the common case. BLOCKED (na-9tk): quipu_context and quipu_hybrid_search need vectors; quipu knot does not embed, --embed-backfill fails with 'No embedding provider configured', --features onnx gives the runtime not a model, and huggingface.co is not on the cloud Trusted allowlist so the model cannot be fetched from a session. Documented in quipu-integration.md. 12 new tests; 189 pass with a live quipu 0.3.11.

title: K3: learned memory write and recall
description: Postgame extraction to mem: episodes, bitemporal per-game and durable, tactics into the prompt. Exit: a tactic learned in game N surfaces in game N+1. K3.

title: Record a real game into a world-view store
description: Once the fixture and harness exist, run a game with NA_WORLD_VIEW_STORE set and commit the harvested world views as orchestrator fixtures. The store and replay machinery landed with na-10f; this is the half that needs a game.

title: A1: POST the world view and apply Claude's build choice
description: First end-to-end LLM decision in a real game. Wraps mod_base_build to serialize state to the contract, call POST /decide, and apply the returned action. Keep the DLL thin.
notes:
DESIGN SETTLED 2026-07-29. Input requirements are specified per-category in the new docs/decision-inputs.md section 2 - build the world view to that checklist, not ad hoc.

Orchestrator side ALREADY EXISTS: service.py serves POST /decide taking a WorldView and returning
Orders (contract.py). So A1 is DLL-side work only.

Item encoding (thinker src/base.cpp): item_id >= 0 is a unit proto id, item_id < 0 is a facility
with id -item_id, range 1..SP_ID_Last=133. So action ids should be 'unit:<proto>' and
'facility:<id>' - reversible, and it keeps engine ids out of the contract as bare integers.

Action space must be engine-authoritative via can_build(base_id, item) and
can_build_unit(base_id, unit) (base.h:68-69). Never synthesise an option. Enrich each Action with
mineral cost, turns at current surplus, category and a one-line effect - contract.Action is
extra=allow so this needs no schema change. A bare name list is not a decidable comparison and
will bias the brain toward expensive items.

Gate: ask on call_seq == 1 only and reuse the answer for the rest of the base-turn (see
thinker 73fbdbc). One decision, one record, one paid call.

Fallback is the feature, not the error handler: on timeout, transport failure, malformed response,
or an action_id outside the offered space, return native_choice and mark the record degraded.
Wire it from the first commit - invariant 9.

Faction scope: narrow llm_factions from 254 to a single slot. Per the faction-gate commit
rationale, prefer a human slot with manage_player_bases=1 over an AI slot, because an AI slot
silently inherits difficulty handicaps and makes any outcome uninterpretable.

Still to build in the DLL: an HTTP client (none exists - net.cpp is a stub and only user32/gdi32/
winmm/psapi are linked; plan is raw ws2_32 for 127.0.0.1 rather than wininet, which is slow and
quirky under Wine), world-view serialisation, minimal JSON response parsing, and the apply path.

title: Replay mode and determinism diffing
description: Observability step 7. Feed stored world views back through a changed orchestrator with no game running and diff the decisions. Determinism diffing only holds for scripted-brain runs; real-model runs need the weaker assertion of same surfaces fired and same legality.
close_reason: Machinery landed and tested; recording a real game is na-oh5. Dropped the na-04z dependency: the replay path needs stored world views, not an adapter that stamps surface_id -- that was a mis-specified blocker. replay.WorldViewStore is content-addressed by the record's own world_view_hash (the blocker found on starting was that the record carries only the hash and nothing kept the bytes, so a log alone could never be replayed). Two verdicts kept separate: deterministic (exact, scripted only) and consistent (no new degradation, same surfaces fired) -- the trap is a replay where the fallback happens to pick what the brain picked. Wired as NA_WORLD_VIEW_STORE, 'neural-amplifier replay' and 'just replay', plus stored() for fixture harvesting.

title: OpenTelemetry exporter fed from the same emit call
description: Observability step 6. Layer 2. Earns its keep because Quipu and Hank are separate services and without shared trace context a slow turn cannot be attributed. Must be fed from the single DecisionLog.write call, never assembled twice.
close_reason: Layer 2 landed in orchestrator/src/neural_amplifier/telemetry.py. Emitter takes the already-built DecisionRecord and hands the same instance to every sink, so 'assembled once' is structural -- the test asserts object identity, not field equality. DecisionLog is just the first sink and is written first, so an exporter failure still leaves the record of truth on disk; sinks never raise into the decision loop and failures are counted on Emitter.failures and surfaced at GET /health. OtelSink continues the adapter's W3C traceparent rather than starting a new trace (dependency-free strict parser, 10 malformed cases rejected), reconstructs span timing from latency_ms since the decision is already over, sets ERROR status on degradation, and emits the section 6 metrics with a bounded-cardinality attribute subset. Enabled with NA_OTEL=1 and the otel extra. 27 new tests against an in-memory tracer -- no collector, no game. Also fixed a real crash path: _record read world_view.trace.traceparent, which AttributeErrors on a model_copy-constructed view and would stall the game after the decision; now WorldView.traceparent() tolerates both shapes.

title: Adapter stamps surface_id and traceparent on the world view
description: Observability step 5. The adapter's entire telemetry job: two fields on the payload it already sends, plus the fairness block. Export stays in the orchestrator because the DLL must not block the game message pump. docs/observability.md section 4.

title: Ask upstream Quipu for VALUES support
description: Filed upstream as scbrown/quipu#51 (VALUES) and #52 (FILTER IN). quipu 0.3.11 rejects both -- 'unsupported graph pattern' and 'unsupported FILTER expression'. We build a || disjunction instead, which works but is O(n) in query text and gets unwieldy past a few dozen action-space items. Close this when either lands upstream and we can simplify datalinks/quipu.py build_query().

title: Parse the remaining alphax.txt sections
description: K1 covers TECHNOLOGY, FACILITIES (incl. secret projects), WEAPONS and DEFENSES. CHASSIS (four name+gender pairs before the numeric fields), UNITS, REACTORS, ABILITIES, TERRAIN, RESOURCEINFO and the SOCIO tables share the file but not the shape, and were skipped rather than half-parsed. Each needs its own row reader plus the smac: classes from knowledge-architecture.md.

title: Bounded deny-repair loop for guard denials
description: knowledge-architecture.md specifies deny-violations returned to the model for bounded repair (max 2 retries, then end_turn). Current behaviour is strip-then-degrade, which is correct but gives up a turn the model could have salvaged.

title: Investigate auto_play_callback as the unattended driver
description: 0x50E890, thinker src/engine.cpp:638. Looks like SMAC's own autoplay hook and may answer what occupies the remaining human slot during an unattended run. Cheap to check during the harness work.
close_reason: Negative result: auto_play_callback is NOT the unattended driver. Zero call sites in the fork (engine.cpp:638 declares the pointer, nothing invokes it), and 0x50E890 sits inside a contiguous block of void(int) GUI timer callbacks -- mandate_color 0x50E820, then blink_timer 0x50EA40, blink2_timer, line_timer, turn_timer (its int annotated 'unused'), go_timer. Siblings are patched at GUI offsets and reimplemented in gui.cpp (mod_blink_timer, mod_turn_timer at patch.cpp:445,1158). This is SMAC's attract-mode/animation tick; the name is misleading. headless-harness.md section 7 Q2 updated to say so and to point at load_daemon + cmd_parse + mod_auto_save instead.

title: Fog-gate the AI-to-AI diplomacy feed
description: mod_NetMsg_pop sees all foreign treaty changes; a faction should not know about pacts between factions it has never met. Filter on contact before it enters the world view or it is an information cheat. docs/headless-harness.md section 4.2.
close_reason: Gated orchestrator-side in fog.py. redact() drops any delta naming a faction outside the world view's new contacts list, before the brain call -- a redaction applied after the prompt would be theatre, and the test asserts the brain never saw it. Deltas naming no parties are public news and survive; the viewing faction is implicitly contacted. Removals are counted on the decision record (redacted_deltas) and aggregated in coverage, so a leaking adapter shows up as a number rather than as a suspiciously well-informed run. A world view without contacts sets fog_enforced=false rather than reporting clean -- we cannot distinguish a legitimate delta from a leaked one, so absence of evidence is recorded as such. Contract gained contacts; headless-harness.md section 4.2 documents the gate. 10 tests. Adapter-side filtering at mod_NetMsg_pop is still the right first line and belongs with A1.
